utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone. Mr. Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning to everyone in the courtroom. This is case number IT-06-90-T, The Prosecutor versus Ante Gotovina, et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Good morning, Mr. Dawes. I would like to remind you that the solemn declaration you gave at the beginning of your testimony still binds you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe, the Chamber has not finally made up its mind as far as one or two sessions. We'll further consider the matter after we have had an opportunity to follow your cross-examination during the first session. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. Mr. Registrar, if we could go back to P62 on the screen.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was wondering if I could get my hard copy back.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I think that would be a good thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: New, Mr. Dreyer [sic], good morning -- excuse me, Mr. Dawes.

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good to start off on the right foot.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. Mr. Dawes, let's go back to the trip you took with Mr. Dreyer on the morning of the 4th. Looking at your statement, P980, at page 5 at the top, and using the marker, sir, could you mark on the map that is before you, Mr. Dawes, the location where in 1996 you put these bomblets. Well, let's read it together at the top of the page. Do see where it is? It stays: "During the trip, we kept the tops open on the APC to be able to look for UN personnel. When we passed 150 metres south from the main crossing in the centre of Knin, going in the direction towards the bus station, we discovered that most of the tree tops along the alley were cut; however not too much damage was seen at the bottom of those trees. We then saw the bomblets, small bombs from a cluster bomb," and then you mention that you had and Mr. Dreyer looked at it. Now, let us first mark -- apologies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The problem that arises, Mr. Kehoe, is that we see that the interpreters then start reading and translating, and then sometimes even portions are missing. I would like to urge you to slow down when reading. If you'd put your question to the witness, we could continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, apologies to the Court apologies to the interpreters.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, first, Mr. Dawes, I would like you to mark with the letter [sic] "1" the main crossing in the centre of Knin?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you blow that map up a little bit better, or just the general area is fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: No, we can blow it that up better. That will be fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe, I think that Madam Usher is seeking your guidance.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. Dawes, is that sufficient or would you like it blown up yet further, sir?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that is sufficient.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes. With the assistance of the usher, if we could just have that marked.

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: In that general area.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So we have that marked with the number 1.

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sorry. My 1 is a little bit crooked, but that's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: That's quite all right, sir. Now, in 1996, you noted that the bomblets were 150 metres south of the main crossing in the centre of Knin going in the direction towards the bus station. Where was that? Could you circle that area and put a "2" in it?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And that would be a tree-lined area along the main road. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: If my memory serves me well, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And if we can turn your attention to page 6 of your statement, the -- not the lead-over paragraph but the carry-over paragraph. But the first full paragraph says: "After we returned to the camp without further incident, I saw the bomblets were still in the main street." In 1996, you're talking about the same location where you named as number 2? Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe so.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let us return to D862. Your Honour, at this time, I will -- actually, if I can -- do I need to -- just procedurally, Judge, I want to go back to this map. Can I move to another location and then come back to this, or do I need to solidify this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think, if we move to another exhibit, that this should one be stored in one way or another.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you want it play or show anything in Sanction, it can be done simultaneously. If you want to move to another picture -- if this is played there Sanction, there is no problem; otherwise, we have to store it first, and then we can restore it at a later stage and even add markings.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: With the Court's permission, if can store those initial markings, then I would like to come back to it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then, Mr. Russo, I take it there is no objection against that. We have it MFI'd; that is, the aerial view on Knin marked by the witness in relation to the bomblets. Thank you, Mr. Registrar, that would be ...

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this becomes Exhibit number D863, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, if we can just go to D862, Mr. Dawes, that is a film made on the 4th of August by Zastava Films, a Serb film service. Did you know that Zastava Films was out on the street on the 4th of August filming various aspects of the shelling of Knin?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: We viewed this yesterday, if we could just look at this quickly, and we can talk while it playing.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If we can display this.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. Dawes, this is the location that you identified as number 2 in your chart that we just looked at it, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would have no idea.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Russo.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There are many tree-lined streets in Knin.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Examine this street, Mr. Dawes. How many streets in Knin remotely resemble this street that you spent -- in a city that you spent from May of 1994 till October of 1995?

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm going to object to that question. How many street remotely resemble this? I don't think that is a clear enough.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: It is clear as it possibly could be. I am putting on the table any street in the town of Knin --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe, I think Mr. Russo was addressing me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you would do the same, that would certainly help. Yes, the question may be answered. If you can answer the question, the question is rather broad, but if you think that you can give us a number of streets, which remotely resemble what we see here, please tell us. If you can't, please tell us as well.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sir, I would have no way to ascertain if that was the street in question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, sir, in 2008, you changed the locations, didn't you, where you saw -- allegedly saw bomblets.

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let us go back to -- before we go to that, let us go back to P984. Before we go back to this, can we go back to P984. I don't know if this is the digitally-enhanced version or not. I turn to my learned friend ... [Overlapping speakers]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It is not. It's the old one. Let's work with it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I think we have it via Sanction, Judge. Can we --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We can work with it for the time being if the witness can see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Can you see the location as "I"?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And what is location is that? How did you identify "I"?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that is where I saw the overturned police vehicle.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let us go back to the item that we've stored. I believe I have notification that the stored item is D863 for MFI.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Going back to this area, you just noted for us that the area "I" is where you saw the overturned vehicle. You told us -- you said, in 1996, the bomblets were in area that you listed as "2." Where were these bomblets, allegedly, that you saw?

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I could.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Excuse me.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: I'm addressing the Court, please. I'm addressing the Court. Your Honour, if I could make an objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe, Mr. Russo may raise an objection if he wishes to do so. Mr. Russo, you be strict in what could be subject of an objection. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I ask that the witness in being referred to what he marked as "I" on P --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: This is exactly --

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I object to the speaking objection --

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: I am wait making an objection. Please wait.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: This is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we restore, Mr. Kehoe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Judge, with all due respect --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe, with all due respect, you should calm down.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: With all due respect, I understand what counsel is doing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I first asked you to calm down, and not just to continue as you did. Is that clear?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Then we'll ask you -- Mr. Dawes, I, unfortunately, have to ask to you leave the courtroom for a second --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- so that the gentlemen can address me without your presence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Russo.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. My objection was to -- with respect to the witness being shown P984, asking him to describe what the marking under letter "I" represents. I was going to object to the fact that he was not directed to the portion of his statement, the supplemental statement, the 2008 statement, which indicates what "I" represents. He clearly remembers a portion of it and not the other portion of it. I was simply looking for the witness, as I think is appropriate, to be directed to what he said regarding that, and not to do what I think Mr. Kehoe is doing in attempting to -- he wants to indicate what is indicated in paragraph 16 of P981, I believe it is. If not correct, that's fine, but I think it is unfair to the witness to ask him what the "I" represents and not show him what he said "I" represents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Your Honour, the Defence is entitled to challenge the credibility and the reliability of what this witness has to say. This witness 13 or 12 years after the fact, in 199 -- excuse me, in 2008 miraculously changes a location for these alleged bomblets, which, by the way, nobody else talks about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Let's then -- why not say to the witness, "In your statement, you said that the bomblets were there. Today, you tell us the bomblets are here. What causes this?"

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: My question -- my goal here is, as we sit here -- and mind you, Judge, this is several months after he gave this statement to the Office of the Prosecutor where he said where this was, if I may, P981 is April of 2008.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But no one is denying you an opportunity to just put to the witness that there's an inconsistency or a contradiction. Why not do that? Why do in a way in which every starts feeling uncomfortable, emotional? I mean, the matter seems to be entirely --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I can tell you exactly why, Judge, because when you lie, your memory is faulty as to what you said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. That's -- let's put it to the witness that there is a contradiction. When you lie, we have not -- a lie means intentionally telling not the truth. A lie and a mistake are not exactly the same. You are here, and it's your duty to point at inconsistencies. And if you later want to address the Court and say, "Well, Mr. Dawes is lying," fine. No problem. But let's go to the issue that is that there is not -- that there is an inconsistency, there is a contradiction in statements; and then if you want to put focussed question to him, "Did you intentionally ..." Ask him for an explanation. We'll hear his explanation. It might turn out that it was a lie; it might turn out that it was an error; whatever it is. But let's keep things simple and quiet.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, may I just comment just briefly? Issues of contradict, Your Honour, are never simple, and simply what happens often in cross-examination on credibility, it is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If I may --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. Mr. Kehoe, I think I gave you my guidance. The Court, and we have discussed this yesterday, wants to avoid that this courtroom becomes a debating club. You have my guidance, and you can put it in the way I suggested to you to the witness. You also know what happens if, finally, the examination-in-chief or the cross-examination takes a course, which the Chamber considers inappropriate; then the supervisory role of this Court will finally result in the Court putting the questions which it feels that the parties apparently want to put to the witness. The witness can be brought in again.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I could -- my apologies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Russo.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Your Honour, in line with what Your Honour and Mr. Kehoe is saying, I would just like to direct the Court's attention to yesterday's transcript, page 10.483, beginning at line 22. The aerial photo of Knin, P62, was put up for the witness. Mr. Kehoe asked him to indicate where, in 1996, he saw the bomblets. He took the blue pen, as can you see in there. He put a marking where "I" was on the subsequent statement. You'll see from reading the transcript that the witness says: "Well, that's where I recollect ..." Then is cut off, saying: "No, no, no, sir," and then moved back to focussing on something else. So when the witness was asked again yesterday by Mr. Kehoe where he recollects these bombs being, he was marking the same location "I," and then he was cut off and then taken back to his statement and asked again.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Your Honour, my next question to him was going to be, before the objection arose, as to where he allegedly saw these bomblets. That was the next question, and have him mark it on the chart.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think Mr. Russo is referring to yesterday's transcript --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I understand, Judge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- and is drawing our attention to the fact that where the witness was asked yesterday about this, that he was interrupted. That's what Mr. Russo did, and that is apart from what was the next question you have on your mind for today.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes. And on that score -- and I'm glad that counsel brought that up, because it makes what the witness just said minutes ago even more alarming, because "I," he says, is the overturned vehicle. And "I" is where he saw the bomblets, and here he says it is where the overturned vehicle was. It is clear at this point that the witness has no idea what he said even most recently, but we will give him that opportunity as soon as he comes back in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you'd do it quietly and calmly, so as not to disturb the atmosphere in this courtroom, you're entitled to do so. Mr. Kuzmanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I know this has arisen oftentimes in cross-examination, and I just wanted to add to the record and make it perfectly clear that if the witness has a problem or is confused or doesn't understand, the witness can ask for either his ability to clarify or he doesn't understanding something. What bothers me, as a Defence attorney in cross-examination, is the fact that the Prosecution is, in this particular instance, rises and is basically instructing the witness what to do through his objection. That is the problem here, Your Honour, not necessarily that the witness is -- that anybody it trying to trap the witness or to fool the witness or to pull something over the witness' eyes. If the witness doesn't understand the question, if the witness is confused, the witness is an adult, he is somebody who has been in that situation, it's not a child we're dealing. The witness can ask for clarification or for a copy of his statement. The whole purpose of objecting is to see whether the question is perhaps improperly made or there is some evidentiary reason to make the objection, and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kuzmanovic --

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: -- that's what is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- I appreciate your observations. You may remember that when I allowed Mr. Russo to make an objection, that I added to that specifically that he should stay within the limits of what is appropriate in making an objection, and once --

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: I do understand, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And once this resulted in the, could I call it, the mini-chaos, I asked the witness to leave the courtroom, exactly for the reasons you have drawn my attention to.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: I appreciate that Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So I hope you feel that it's in safe hands.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: I do. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then, Mr. Russo, there is some merit in what Mr. Kuzmanovic just said. I even add to that, that I observed similar things happening during, not specifically with this witness, with the examination-in-chief. Sometimes, I also got the impression that too easily an objection was placed where there was no need yet. We now have discussed that there are certain contradictions, there are inconsistencies. There's no problem in exploring them, but let's do it calmly, let's do it focussed. And if, Mr. Kehoe, you would also keep in mind what happened yesterday, as Mr. Russo has drawn our attention to. Then, I will ask the usher, who had fled the courtroom, to bring in the witness again. And, Mr. Kehoe, yesterday I made a reference to Friday emotions and Monday emotions, and I have to add Tuesday emotions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Judge, I'm look this 24/7.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Dawes, the apology is that you had to leave the courtroom because, to some extent, emotions -- there was a risk that emotions would take over. That risk, I hope, has now been reduced. Mr. Kehoe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. Dawes, going back to the --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Sorry, apologies.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. Dawes, going back to the exhibit on the screen. So where in this location, if you could mark it with "3," did you now say that you observed these alleged bomblets?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: I want to be clear, Your Honour, on this point, and I don't want to frustrate the Defence. I cannot clearly remember the exact location where I've seen these cluster bombs. I can remember two locations, and I'm not sure which one it is, and that's about as candid as I can be. I know in my statement from 1996 that I say it's at the location I circled with the "2" on the map, and then I know I have said on other occasions that it may have been around where that Serbian police car was overturned down by the Tvik screw factory. I cannot remember which location they were at.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this time, we will offer into evidence the exhibit that is on the screen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Russo.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: No objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then Exhibit D863, which was MFI'd, is now admitted into evidence. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. Dawes, I know you're not a military person, but do you know whether or not the HV even had a weapon system at that time that was able to fire any type of bomblets like this?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I do not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Do you know if the ARSK possessed that weapons system?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I do not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Are you familiar with the type of weapons system that the ARSK fired on Zagreb in May of 1995?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not really. I just knew that they lobbed a couple of -- I thought they were artillery rounds into Zagreb.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Do you have any recollection, sir, that they were bomblets?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: No --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: -- cluster bomblets?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I do not remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: When you observed what you allegedly observed, did you talk to Mr. Dreyer about this?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember 100 percent, but I believe I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And going to the top of page 5, would that be the conversation that you talk with Dreyer about, commenting that you stay away from the bomblets?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember making the statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Did you file any reports on seeing these bomblets, sir, when you got back to headquarters?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Your Honour, last night, I accepted -- asked the Prosecution for a stipulation that Mr. Dreyer did not talk about these bomblets in either his statements the before the Court or in his statement, and the Prosecution has accepted that stipulation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then it's on the record now, Mr. Russo.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. Dawes, let's me move to your second trip, okay? And I believe that in your second trip, you noted that - and this is again on page 5 - that you left the camp somewhere around 8.15 and 8.30. I'm referring to, if you can just take a look, page 5. Can you see that, sir?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And you note in had a sequence that there was anti-personnel mines put out prior to that time. Do you see that in that first paragraph?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: "While back in the UN camp, two RSK soldiers ..." Is that where you are referring to?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Just if you could read that to yourself.

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certainly. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So before you left the camp on the second trip, these mines were put out in front of the gate?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So if you left the camp between 8.15 and 8.30, it would have to have been sometime prior to that?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would believe so.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: How many times during the course of that day -- well, let me rephrase that. Was this the only indication - only time, I should say - that the ARSK put mines out in front of the gate of UN Sector South?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's the only one that I remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let me show you D5. This is an UNMO report from the 4th at 1600.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And if we could go to the second page, at the urgent, urgent info section.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If you can read, 1: "From 1515 Bravo, Sector South headquarters is blockaded by ARSK. Anti-tank mines laid on the main road to Knin, 100 metres from the HQ entrance gate." Now that notes, Mr. Dawes, that this event took place at 1515 Bravo, or 3.15 in the afternoon. That is well after your timing on this second trip, is it not?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Seems to be.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, if we can go back to -- just staying on that, is it clear to you, sir, as you sit here, that the timing that you've given this Trial Chamber of when and where you did things is accurate?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the best of my ability. Specifically about the mine thing, I believe I was well inside the camp after 1530 on my third and last trip. If ARSK soldiers put the mines back, I would have no knowledge of that because I wasn't by the -- by the gate. It could be another occurrence is what I'm say.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And one would think, would you not, that such an occurrence, if it happened more than once, would be in some Sector South reporting, wouldn't it?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: One would assume so.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let us bring up on the screen P -- excuse me, D856.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, this is going to the route that you took the second time, Mr. Dawes, just in frame of reference. Now looking at 856, D856, you left the Sector South headquarters and went to Potkonje. Is that right? That's over to the right as you come out.

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: In that general direction, for sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yeah. And at this location, you note in your statement that you had -- or met 12 to 15 armed RSK soldiers. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And they were holding UN personnel hostage.

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Definitely.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, what unit were these RSK soldiers a part of; do you know?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: No idea.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, this is, in fact, the second time in several hours that you saw groups of RSK soldiers in the town. Would that be accurate?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: That would be the second time I saw a group of with RSK soldiers, one in Knin and the other outside the Knin.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And this outside the Knin, approximately how far is Potkonje from downtown Knin?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: From downtown Knin or from the garrison?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Just from the garrison?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Two clicks, two and a half clicks.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And how far is the garrison from downtown Knin?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Same distance, I would say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now for me, clicks is not an expression I'm familiar with.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Kilometres.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Kilometres. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. Dawes, I know what you meant, but my colleague didn't. Now, the next indication in your reports of RSK soldiers is in page 6 of your 1996 statement, where you talk about with RSK soldiers with lightly wounded coming from the direction of Strmica. Do you see that, sir?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, if we can go, and if we can put up P62 on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Again, sir, using the marker, when you say that you observed these four RSK trucks coming from the direction of the Strmica road, can you mark with an arrow the road that you're talking about that you believed these four ARSK trucks were travelling?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah. Yes, I can, to answer your question. You want the direction the trucks were travelling in.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let me just be clear, I want a frame of reference where you say from the direction of the Strmica road. So if you could give the Chamber an arrow, in blue, where you saw them coming from and where you observed this.

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: What you can't see on that map is, where you see the town Knin labelled, there's an intersection just to the top of that map. You turn right to go to Vrlika; you turn left to go to Strmica.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, sir, where you put the arrow, is that the approximate path that they were following?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this time, we can offer this item into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: No objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this becomes Exhibit number D864.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D864 is admitted into evidence. Could I seek one clarification. You talked about what we couldn't see on the map; that is, that just above what is on the top of this map. You said you turn right to go to Vrlika. May I take it coming from Knin, because it --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Coming from Knin, you turn right for Split, left for Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now that was the third observation you made of ARSK soldiers according to the statement that you make in the morning of the -- sorry. That was the third observation you made of ARSK soldiers during the morning hours of the 4th. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe so, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let us continue down on that same paragraph on the 6th, where you talk about the ear-ring brigade. Now, you note that you saw the ear-ring brigade which were some of the best units in the area, and you observed them at the intersection downtown. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour. Sorry. The question wasn't finished, but I have an objection.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I heard the question to be: "Is that right?" So, therefore, I thought the question was finished.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I thought Mr. Kehoe was still talking, but if the question is finished, I'd like to object. I believe it indicates that he saw soldiers from the ear-ring brigade, not the entire ear-ring brigade. I think that is a distinction that needs to be made.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: With all due respect, Mr. Dawes, I did not mean to mislead you, and the report does say "some." If I misled anybody by my question, I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's proceed, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So saw some ARSK soldiers from this ear-ring brigade?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, you noted that this ear-ring brigade was one of the best ARSK units in the area?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: How did you know that?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: From living in town, from stopping at enough check-points, general folklore.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And, again, in the morning hours of the 4th, that is the fourth separate viewing of you of ARSK soldiers in and around Knin, right?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is the fourth time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If I can just have one second, Judge.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, your third trip, sir, which was D857.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If we could just change to D857.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, this is the trip, sir, where Mr. Engleby went to get you -- went with you. Did you go pick up Mr. Engleby's girlfriend on this trip?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sergeant Engleby.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Excuse me. Sergeant Engleby?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. We tried to pick her up.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And that would have been Christina Roskovic?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: I forget her maiden name, Christina Engleby.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, this also is the trip where you, during the course of your testimony on direct, mentioned that there was mortar rounds landing in and around the ECMM headquarters.

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Do you know if the HV was in range at that time to be able to hit the ECMM headquarters with mortar rounds?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Specifically with mortar rounds, no, I do not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Had you heard during the course of the 4th from any elements in the United Nations that the ARSK had fired on individuals who were part of the United Nations during the 4th of August?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: It's accurate to say, is it not, that you have no idea who fired those mortar rounds that almost hit you, do you?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: No idea.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, during the course of picking up this UN personnel, approximately just in your taskings, how many UN personnel were picked up?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just inside my APCs?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Just inside yours, approximately. You don't have to give us an exact number.

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Anywhere between 30 and 50 maybe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And do you know how many UN personnel total were picked up by the APCs throughout the day?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not. Not all of them, I know. We left some of them downtown on the night of the 4th.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, it's accurate to say, Mr. Dawes, that no UN personnel were injured as a result of the shelling on the 4th or the 5th, were they?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Physically injured?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would have no idea. Not to my recollection. Do you know UN personnel as also locals, or do you know internationals.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, certainly, let's start with the internationals?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not to my knowledge. As to the locals, I would not know because many of them did not come on to the camp.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Suffices it to say, at this point, you know of nobody that was injured?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Physically.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: You noted during the course of your -- and I'm talking now about the shelling itself of Knin, and turning to paragraph 24 of P981, the second sentence: "I would like to add that when I saw the smoke clear from the town ..." --

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: What page are you on, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I'm on page -- paragraph 24 of your 2008 statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Page 5 out of six.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Oh, excuse me. Page 5 out of six, paragraph 24. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: You noted that you are surprised that: "The damage did not appear to be that severe compared to the shelling I had experienced while in town." As you sit here in 2008, Mr. Dawes, and you reflect back, you have come to two conclusions, have you not; one, that you do not believe that anything was wrong with the shelling, and, two, that the HV was not targeting civilians. Isn't that right? Isn't that what you told Mr. Stanton?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember specifically I said to Mike. I recognised that there was a war was going on and that the Croatians were retaking their land. I identified that, I believe. Secondly, I was amazed that when the dust settled and the smoke cleared on them, the next day the town looked significantly better than the last time I saw it during the morning of the 4th.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And based on that, sir, you have concluded that you didn't think there was anything wrong with the shelling, and that the HV was not targeting civilians. Isn't that what you concluded?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not remember saying that at all, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, as you sit here, is that your conclusion, as you sit here today?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it is not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let us talk a bit about the refugee issue coming into the camp, and you noted that you were the person who was searching these refugees in the camp. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not directly searching. I was overseeing some of the process of that. I wasn't physically patting people down or emptying their purses out or anything like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I apologise, sir. Are you the person, sir, that was telling them that they had to be searched?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't speak the local lingo, so I don't know if I was telling them. I may have been asking an interpreter to tell them that. I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was definitely a policy for us to have the refugees searched before the entered into the camp for weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, it was during this time-frame, was it not, that Colonel Leslie told you that the UN had either given or were going to give fuel to the ARSK soldiers to help them flee Sector South. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Did you know if he conveyed this information that they were going to give fuel to ARSK soldiers, if he conveyed that information to General Forand?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm way down the food chain. I would not be privileged to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let me show you an incident, D513, and I ask you if you're aware of it. Let me ask you, without even going into that, were you aware of an incident - and I'm talking about an incident, if I can date this for you - on the 13th of July, were you aware of an incident where Colonel Leslie agreed to give 500 litres of diesel and 100 litres of petrol to the ARSK in return for an observation post, and that the SC, Sector Commander, was not informed and will be kept in the dark, only a few people will know about this deal. Were you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now --

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I may add, if Colonel Leslie wanted to have an observation post, there was a normal process for that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's not further explain. You have no knowledge on the matter Mr. Kehoe asked about and, therefore, I think he will put next question to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Turning to the actual bringing of the refugees in, and turning to page 7 of your statement, 980, not the carry-over paragraph, but the second full paragraph, last sentence. Do you see that? "My task ..."

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of my 1996 statement?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: On page 7?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Page 7.

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Second paragraph?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: The second full paragraph, not the carry-over paragraph, but the second full paragraph, beginning with, "The shelling commenced," and then the last sentence: "The General decided ..."

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And that notes that your task was to tell the people they were about to be searched. Now --

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: May I just say something about the General? I may have been referred to Leslie at that time, because I believe he was a General at that time. This was -- so I'm not sure whether it was Forand or Leslie.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Understood. In any event, sir, as these people were coming in, you told them, either directly or through an interpreter, that they had to be searched?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And let me just show you briefly D748, and I'll show you a couple of documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I said D748. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let me just talk about it while we're bringing this up. During the course of this, were you present at the gate when this transpired, when these people were coming in?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Off and on. We would take shifts.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Did you see that the search was taking place, that weapons were being taken off these individuals?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard weapons that there were weapons taken off. I believe there was a handgun and a grenade was taken off some people. I wasn't there for that, though.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Were you aware that soldiers were let in during that period of time?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: I definitely know that there was fighting-age males let in at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And how many fighting-age males were let in at that time?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would not know the number, but there were a lot of males inside the camp.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, just briefly talking about your statement and going to page 4 in your 1996 statement, you refer very briefly when you talking about the young ARSK soldiers -- I'm talking about the first full paragraph, not the carry-over paragraph. About midway down, you say that you ran into some RSK soldiers. The next sentence: "Some of them seem to have left the front lines to get their families out of the region as soon as possible. Later, some of them even tried to get into the camp." Do you see that sentence?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, is that referring to the soldiers that you saw on the street that attempted to get into the camp?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Were they let in to the camp?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. They could well have been. I was not there the whole time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Were you aware that people were taken from the hospital and brought into the camp?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am aware of that now, but only from talking to other people after the invasion. I wasn't aware during the invasion.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And who did you talk to about that?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember. It was after Storm had finished.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, did they tell that you that the people that had been taken from the hospital and brought into the camp were ARSK wounded soldiers?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I just remember that there was people taken from the hospital into our camp.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: My apologies, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, I would like to turn to the subject, Mr. Dawes, of looting which you talked about at some point yesterday. And you noted for us, I believe it's in your statement, in your supplementary statement, that on the 6th in Knin, the -- actually, what you say is that the looting -- he witnessed on the 6th -- in Knin on the 6th appear to be organised and systematic because the HV soldiers were separating valuable items for loading into military trucks. Do you recall that, sir?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, let us talk preliminarily about what was actually taken here; and at the top of page 3 of your 1996 statement, in the second paragraph, you note: "East of UN headquarters was a logistics base mainly for small-arms. I saw the Croats taking away all those small-arms after Storm." Now, you noticed them taking arms from there.

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: You could see from inside our camp right down into that camp.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I understand. Did they take other items from that camp?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would assume so.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So they would -- in addition to that, you were aware of the fact that the northern barracks -- you mentioned to us that you were in the northern barracks?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Did the HV take items out of the northern barracks?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: That would be a logical conclusion.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: You were aware of the Senjak barracks across from the Tvik factory, are you not?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am aware that there was -- may have been a military facility there, but I have never entered it myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, based on what you saw, would you included that the HV took items out of that base as well?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And you know that they had a headquarters downtown, that the ARSK had a headquarters downtown?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that the government had a headquarters downtown.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Would it, likewise, be logical based on what you saw that the HV would take items from that location?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So you would agree with me, sir, that -- that it would be logical that the HV would go into all of the potential military -- or not potential, military facilities in Knin and remove items for their own use?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Logical.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: When you say you observe this on the 6th --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If we could go back to P62.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe, earlier you referred to the, you said, supplementary statement without giving the paragraph number.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: It is a proofing statement, Judge. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Oh, it's a proofing statement, which we are not aware of.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Dawes, again using P62, this blank map, where were you when you observed that the HV was systematically separating these items for loading onto military trucks? Where were you and where did you see this?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: You just want to know where I saw people removing things from buildings or saw vehicles with belongings in them as well?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: You testified on direct examination that there was a systematic -- systematic method of separating valuable items that were put on trucks and from other household items, and this was done by the HV. I'd like to you on this map to, if there are multiple locations, put numbers. But --

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Along that route.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Along that route, that's where you observed it. Let me show you two documents, and we will go through these quickly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If I can just put this chart into evidence before we move on. Your Honour, I'm just offering this into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Russo.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: No objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this becomes Exhibit number D865.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D865 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let me show you two documents, the first being 1D57-0096. I recognise, Mr. Dawes, that you haven't seen this, but I just want to -- for you to look at the content of these two documents. This is a first a report from 11 August 1995 from the chief of the 4th Guards Brigade, and we'll try to briefly go through these pages because we have another document still.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If we can turn the page, you see a multiple of items you see inventory of war booty captured in Oluja, Operation Storm. On the right-hand side, it notes the amount and/or the weight of those items. If we can go to the next page, I have no idea what a foot lubrication device is, but there were two of them. If we can go to the next page, in that page, you see office furniture, chairs. Next page, washing machines, kitchen utensils et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Before we talk about this, Mr. Dawes, I want to show you one more document, so we can move through this as quickly as possible, which is 65 ter 2053. This is a bit of a longer list. This is an inventory of collected war booty items from the 4th Guards Brigade, dated 13 August 1995, going to the Split Military District, personally the commander. Again, talking about list of items seized. If we can just go through this seriatim, it notes some biological and chemical pieces. Next page, pretty much the same thing. Next page.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Just scroll to page 7 in this document. We begin to talk about the seizure of various types of weaponry. Can we go to the next page.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Next page, we get into more specific item, stereos, video recorders, freezers. Next page, talking about trucks, automobiles. Next page, yet more weaponry.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Go two pages up.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Bottom of the page, we notice some vehicles, a Fiat, an Opel?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If we go to the next page.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Again, we notice more trucks. Next page, this includes typewriters, additional radio equipment, refrigerators at the bottom of the page, freezers, gas stove.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Next page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One refrigerator, I take it, you are referring to.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Refrigerator?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You used the plural.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: My apologies. Two freezers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One refrigerator.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If I misspeak, Judge, the document speaks --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: The next page, page 15, is at top of that page, if we can scroll up, we have six TV sets, video recorder, VCR player. Again, towards the bottom of that page, we have a Mercedes and a Lada.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Can we scroll through the next page, and the next page, please. Next page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Again, we have two colour TV sets, a hi-fi system.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Can we go to the next page, and again another page through.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: We see another coloured TV sets.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I know at one point I saw a couple of refrigerators in this, Judge, and that is the one I recall, frankly, where it says two refrigerators at the top.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Continuing on the next page, seven colour TV sets in the command centre, cassette recorders, freezer, another refrigerator, various types of weaponry.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Continuing. Next page, please. Various types of automobile equipment. Next page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Here, we have towards the bottom yet more office furniture, 15 office desks, three chairs.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Next page.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: MR. KEHOE: Again, we've more office furniture at the top, 38 office chairs, canvas; 69 office chairs, wood and meatal?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Go to the next page, and then we go to one last page. I believe there's one last page.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Dawes, these items, such as furniture, TV sets, stereos, et cetera, that you saw on this list, were these the type of items that you saw being separated out systematically by the HV and being put on trucks?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this time, we will offer into evidence 1D57-0096, as well as 65 ter 2053.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Russo.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: No objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, these documents becomes Exhibit number D866 and Exhibit D867, respectively.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D866 and D876 are admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let me -- you noted during the course of going through Knin on the 6th, that you were stopped at a check-point by the military police when you were coming back in. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Okay. Let me -- and, again, you spent sometime in and around the Knin area, up until November -- or October - October, I think it is - October of 1995, and you saw quite a few military police check-point, did you not?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let me show you 65 ter 2747. And, again, I understand that this is not a document that you've seen, Mr. Dawes. I just want you to take a look at the content of the document, so we can discuss it a bit. Now, this is a report from the 5th Company of the 72nd Military Police Battalion out of Sinj.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I notice a mistake in the document, Your Honour, from the -- if we can scroll back up on the page, on the B/C/S. We noticed the B/C/S -- my colleague Mr. Misetic notes that the 5th Company, it notes "Knin," and in the actual B/C/S original, it says "Sinj." So I think we can get that corrected and uploaded for the sake of accuracy.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That would be appreciated.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: This is a document from the 8th of August, 1995, a report on items temporarily confiscated at check-points in the zone of responsibility of the 5th Company of the Military Police, Sinj.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If we could just page through this, at the bottom, it describes the items. If we can go to the top -- can we go to the top of the page.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: You notice Mercedes vehicles, engines.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: The right-hand column, for the sake of clarity, it notes "place where found and seized" and notes the location in Knin where these items -- And I must say, Judge, again, for the sake of accuracy, number 4 on this says "a DVD player. I know that I'm old, but I don't think we had DVD players in 1995. But I do reflect that the actual original says -- if we can go back to four on the first page. It notes that it's a video, as opposed to a DVD. Again, this is a 65 ter document, and maybe we can correct that translation. Maybe we did have DVDs in 1995 and I missed it, but I don't think so. In any event, Judge, if we could just continue on in this page.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: It notes various personal items that you see, as we go down towards the bottom of the page: Television sets, at 10; television sets, at 16; DVD player, at 17.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Continuing on, the next page.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Again, we have, after that favorite accordion, a another couple of TV sets, video recorders, telephones. Again, towards the bottom of that page, 41, we have yet more TV sets. Next page, type writer, stereo system. Again, going towards the bottom of the page, after the weaponry, more stereo system.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Go to the next page.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yet more electronics that were confiscated; 62 is another TV set; an automobile, at 70; cassette player, at 78. Next page, bicycles; another TV set, at 95; type writers, at 102.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Next page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Again, various types of equipment; musical equipment; video cameras; cassette players, at 114; television set, at 124; an automobile, at 127. Next page, more television sets, at 129, 136, 143, 151, 153; as well as some automobiles, at 149, 153, 154. Next page, various types of personal items. Next page, again, yet more electronic equipment, as well as weaponry. Next page, again, more machine equipment; stereo systems, at 213; as well as various vehicles, at 218, 221, 222, and that is all. Now, sir, this particular listing that was confiscated at check-points by the military police, were these the type of items that you saw that were being confiscated by the military police as in and around the Knin area during your stay there?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never saw the military police confiscating items; I saw Croatian soldiers confiscating items.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So, just to clarify, as you were going through, you never observed any of the military police stopping vehicles and confiscating items from them?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw them stopping vehicles; I never saw them confiscating items.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this time, we will offer into evidence 65 ter 2747.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Russo.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this becomes Exhibit number D868.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D868 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If I might have one moment, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, sir, when you went out on the 6th, you did observe on the 6th that civilians were looting as well, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: There may have been some civilians looting.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And, certainly, when you were talking about looting, the -- did you make a determination or did you conclude that these were civilians that had come back into the area and were looting items?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, because the Croatian military police was very strict for the first couple of days or -- sorry, the first week, for allowing civilians from the coast to come back into the former RSK.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, let me show you P352.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe, I noted that the columns four and five were not translated in the documents we just admitted into evidence. The translation we only find the -- you have seen that?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I do see that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps with the assistance --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: We'll get it --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. It would not take much, it is just numbers to be added, unless the parties would agree that we can -- that they are of lesser importance, and that the purpose of tendering this document into evidence is to find a description of the type of items that were seized.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Your Honour, my preference would be not to agree to that. The Prosecution will be certainly arguing with respect to the number of items represented on the document, but we will work with the Defence to have that corrected.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm not talking about numbers. I'm not talking about numbers, but talking about I think the indications of where they were seized exactly, and that is not filled in for all the items. I'm not talking, again, not about numbers because they are translated. Mr. Russo, would you consider that, because otherwise it will be an additional effort which, if it doesn't bring us anything, of course would should be avoided.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Certainly, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We would like to hear from you, Mr. Kehoe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Your Honour, in the spirit -- this is an OTP document. In the spirit of making it as accurate as possible, we will take any steps to do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Turning your attention to the report that is on -- this is an UN Sector South sitrep of the 6th of August, the first day that you say you got out.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And if I go to the last page, in paragraph F of the last page -- I'm sorry, the second-to last page. Apologies. If we can blow up paragraph F, five lines down.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: The writer of the Sector South sitrep notes: "More civilians including cars with Split licence plates are seen in Knin." Was that your experience as well, Mr. Dawes, that there were more civilian in Knin as early as the 6th of August driving around with vehicles with Split licence plates?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember seeing that, Mr. Kehoe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: You do recall, sir, that when you were going onto the Drnis road on the 8th - and I refer to your statement, P980, at page 10, fourth paragraph down, second sentence - "Soldiers and civilians were looting the houses all along the road." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do now.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And "soldiers," you mean people that were in camouflage dress right?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean they were in full -- from headgear to footgear, they were in uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And the soldiers were in the same locale as the civilians, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: It seems to be, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And you know of no military operation, authorised military operation, where soldiers and civilians operate together in this fashion, do you?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Your Honour, if we can -- I'm going to move subjects here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I am looking at the clock, if you are -- let me just try to understand you. You said moving.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You're moving to another subject.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then, unless you can finish then in two or three minutes, I would rather have a break.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Actually, I can't finish that subject in two or three.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. We'll have a break in two or three minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Sorry, I can't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Oh, you can't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Apologies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll then have a break. Mr. Kehoe, could you tell us approximately how much time you would still need.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: No more than an hour, Judge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Hmm.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: One hour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll consider it. We'll have a break until 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe, the Chamber has considered the time, and unanimously concluded that you would have 45 minutes remaining. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Couple of topics, Mr. Dawes. The first is page 17 of your -- excuse me, page 11 of your 1996 statement. You talk about the killing of Milan Babic. Do you see that, sir?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And in that, you discuss this with two old ladies in the village, who told you that a man wearing an HV uniform with a lightening bolt on his shoulder badge came and shot Milan Babic, and the reason these ladies gave to you was that the HV shoulders demanded two pigs and he refused?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what I was told.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, you told us in direct examination, at page 10.381, line 23 and then it goes to 10.382, line 5, that Milan Babic was a Croat?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So, from the story that you told us, a Croatian soldier went into a Croatian village and shot a Croatian male for not giving the soldiers a pig?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, do you know, sir, whether that was -- I understand the story. Do you know whether or not that that was some payback for some other revenge between these Croats?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So you don't know anything other than what you just told us, that it was a Croat killing a Croat for a pig?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Being told by two other Croatian ladies.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, let me shift gears, sir, if I can, to your trip on the 6th. Now, in your statement on page 8 - and, again, when I say your "statement," I'm talking about area 1996 statement - about three quarters of the way down on page 8, you noted, on going out with Andries Dreyer that: "We were aware of the - this is the second sentence, pardon me - "We were aware of the ongoing looting and wanted to go down to collect our personal kit before the looters." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So you were going down to get your personal belongings, downtown?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Andries Dreyer was going downtown to pick up his. My belongings were on camp already. I had no belongings downtown.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Would you agree with me, that's not what you say in the statement?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So this would be more accurate to say you were going down to get Dreyer's stuff and you were just going along with him. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, this came at a time where there was restriction of movement on the 6th of August. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And you also know that many people tried to get out of the base on the 6th of August and were prevented from doing so, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, before we go into your observations on the 6th, I take it that after you came back on the 6th from your trip to Vrlika and the Krka and Kistanje, et cetera, you came back and told people in the UN what you observed. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would -- I can't remember. That makes natural sense that I would do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Who did you tell?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: No idea.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, let us -- let us talk a little bit about this statement and just taking it seriatim, beginning on the bottom of page 8, you note that you went out of the base and you went in the direction of Drnis to Vrbnik, right? Then you noted that you saw eight to ten bodies that were at a junction that were in body-bags, right? I'm talking about that tame paragraph, right towards the end.

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: You have no idea how these people were killed, do you?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I do not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: You, likewise, have no idea where these bodies came from?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I do not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So, as far as you know, they could have been killed in combat operations or in any other possibilities. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were dead.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Right. Now, you note for us that Vrbnik - and again, I'm talking about on page 8 towards the bottom - you went to Vrbnik and it's a village of approximately 50 houses.

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Spread out. The town of Vrbnik itself is quite small, but there are outlying buildings. Approximately. I would have no idea today.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, tell us a little bit about this trip. You went through Vrbnik, you saw these body-bags at the junction. I take it you didn't stop and examine those body-bags. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: What you observed in Vrbnik was as you were driving through?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Did you stop in Vrbnik?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not that I can recall. Stopped, like got out of the vehicle? We may have stopped the vehicle and paused, but I can't remember that. I do not remember exiting the vehicle.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
