utterances.text: Do you remember stopping the vehicle?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, you say in this item that you saw "a few HV soldiers." Do you see that? "We were wearing civilian clothes and didn't leave the van. We saw a few HV soldiers." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: You have no idea what these HV soldiers were doing, do you?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: You have no idea if they were a member of a unit or were just wearing [Realtime transcript read in error "carrying] camouflage uniform, do you?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I take it, sir, that you didn't stop and talk to these soldiers?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: You just kept driving through?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: How -- that's how you recollect it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, if we go could to your map, if I may.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: This is P --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe, I'm just trying to -- we are at the bottom page 8?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, we are at the bottom much page 8.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: "We sue a few HV soldiers." You said: "You have no idea they were member of a unit or just carrying camouflage uniforms."

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: "Just wearing camouflage."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I don't see the camouflage uniforms here, whether they were wearing camouflage uniforms, did they?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... I can develop that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I mean, you saw --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, I'm just trying to find out what is in his statement and how he recognised them as HV soldiers. The other question, which is not clear, you said: "You had no idea what they were doing." The statement describes that they were carrying TV sets, videos, and other similar items, which is at least an activity.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I understand, Judge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let me develop the first point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Bottom of page 8, is it accurate to say that what you saw was a few individuals with camouflage uniforms on? Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: I say a few -- when I say "HV," I can't recall if I saw if they had insignia on right now, but obviously they would have been in uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And you concluded they were soldiers -- you would conclude that they were soldiers simply based on the fact that they had camouflage on. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And I think told us --

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: A full set of camouflage.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I think you told us that you didn't stop and talk to them?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, with regard to what they were carrying, I mean the TV sets, et cetera, you have no idea at this point if they were inventorying those items similar to the lists that we showed you previously, do you?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no idea if they were cataloguing those items.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, let us --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Sorry, Judge, if that was -- by way of clarity, I trust that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: -- suffices. Let us turn to P983, and if I may just put a larger document in which includes P983 -- if I can just pause one moment, Madam Usher, and replace that request with 1D57-0114. Your Honour, just by way of clarity, this is a multi-page document, and this first page is a blow-up of P983.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, if I may, Mr. Dawes, and -- correct me if I'm wrong at any point, please.

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: No problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: As we take this item, you noted that you went from Vrlika. And I take it, from your statement, you went from Vrlika, going to the bottom of 8, to the Krka monastery, which is listed on the bottom of page 9. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: As a general direction, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So you followed that bottom part of the route, up past the Krka monastery, into Kistanje. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now --

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Can we please just correct the record. I think it indicates, at line 16: "You went from Vrlika. And I take it, from your statement, you went from Vrlika, going to the bottom of 8 ..." And if we're referencing the map, I think that is Vrbnik, not Vrlika.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: You are absolutely right, Mr. Russo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me just see. I had some difficulties in finding the monastery in Krka on the bottom. I see it at the top of page 8 -- 9.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: It will be clear on the next page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, this again is the 6th of August, when the restrictions of movement are in place. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not supposed to be able to leave the camp.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Right. Now, with the clarity that --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I do appreciate that Mr. Russo.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: -- the clarity that Mr. Russo brought to bear, you went to Vrbnik and then you went left on the lower portion of the loop towards Krka monastery, right?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure if it had been a left, but, yeah, okay, that general direction.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: The lower portion?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what you mean by "the lower portion."

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, it's just a circle.

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: You see where Vrbnik is?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, okay. I agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Okay. So going from Vrbnik, you took that road to the left. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Okay. And you took that --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And if we can, go to the next chart, which is again a blow-up of the route that he took. If I may, Your Honour, you see the Krka designated in the circle?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, so you took this road, sir, across, past Krka, and up to Kistanje. Is that the route that you gave?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: How did you get across the river?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: There's a bridge, I believe, to the left of the Krka monastery.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, there is no bridge is there, sir?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe, I was the accommodation officer for Sector South. I travelled that route two or three times a week for over a year. The specifics of the exact dirt road I took, I'm not quite sure; but that is the general direction I went that day.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, you've told us that you took this record that you have put into evidence in the Prosecution's case.

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you go back to the original map, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Excuse me. You told us during your case that you took this road into Kistanje, and the fact is that there is it no such road, is there?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm saying that there is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Okay. Let's go to the next chart in this array. This is the Google Earth item where the Krka monastery is, and I put to you, sir, there is none and never has been any bridge over the Krka River at or about that location, is there?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: When was this Google Earl taken.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I put to you, sir, the question -- do you understand my question have?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe you can say it again.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: My question to you, sir, is that there is and never has been a bring over the Krka River at or about the Krka monastery, is there?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know how to answer your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let's go to the next chart. Maybe that will help.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe, if you put a Google Earth picture to the witness in support of your question, then if the witness says, When was a that one taken," especially if you say "There never has been," then I think it would be appropriate to give an answer to the witness, rather than to, say, don't give the answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I understand, Judge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: This is a Google Earth presentation that can be obtained right now.

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: So it was not taken during the time-frame of Operation Storm?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: No, sir.

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: So what I am telling you, Your Honour, is that that was the route that I took on that day. If you go back to my original route, I can explain how I drew that route, which may add some more levity to the situation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If there's any need to explain that. Let's first wait and see what further questions are put to you by Mr. Kehoe, and if there's then any need to further explore how you put that route on the map, we will give an opportunity to you or we might even ask for it. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Can we go to the next chart in this array, which is a similar angle, with Kistanje up in the left-hand corner and the Krka monastery in the centre of the photograph, with the Krka River running past with no bridge. The next chart.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: This has the actual locations, two locations, of the bridge over the Krka river; area 1 and area 2, respectively.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If we go to the next chart.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Again, the Google Earth matters of the two bridge locations.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And then the next chart.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Using the exhibit that we have, P983, and the location of bridge 1, we have both the designation from P983, as well as the satellite -- Google satellite map that reflects the bridge.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And if we go to the next chart.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: This is the location of bridge 2, the left again in this being the P983 bridge location; and in the circle, it shows the bridge again in the Google Earth.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this time, we will offer into evidence 1D57-0114.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Russo.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would object to all but the first two pages. I don't think the witness has provided any foundation for the remaining exhibits. As a matter of fact, I think he has said he doesn't agree with them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: We will then bar table these documents, Your Honour, for Your Honours' consideration.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And, again, we would object to that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The objection is denied. Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That would be Exhibit D869, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D869 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So going back to the first map in this array, which is P983 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps, in view of the answers the witness has given the questions that you were put to him, that we give him an opportunity now, as he offered earlier, to explain how this route on the map was marked, especially in view of the questions that were put to you. Apparently, the position of the Gotovina Defence is that where you said that you took this route and crossed the river, where there was a bridge, that the apparent position of the Gotovina Defence is that there was no bridge.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sir, back in April, on my way to Afghanistan, I was stopped in The Hague and I shown this map for the first time, I believe, by the Prosecutor. He asked me in April to draw the general area, the route that I took, while matching up with my statement. That map was approximately a metre long by a metre wide; and in a matter of five minutes, I drew the general route I took. I don't believe that that's the best map that I could have been given. If I would have shown an actual map that had all the routes on it, I could have drawn a more accurate map. What I'm telling you is that that is the general area that I drove that day, and I definitely went to Vrbnik, Kistanje, Srb, and Knin in had a curricular way and I bypassed the Krka monastery. That's what I am saying.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Which would then mean that the way marked where you crossed that river might not be accurate; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Kehoe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: As a follow-up to what you just said, you maintain that you went with Andries Dreyer, right?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: I went with Andries Dreyer.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, let us talk a little bit about your first trip into Kistanje, and you noted for us that - and this is again in your statement - that you saw houses marked with "Croatian house" on it. How many houses did you see marked with "Croatian house"?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, can you give us an estimate?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I cannot.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Do you know whether or not any of the -- did you visit Kistanje after the 6th of -- allegedly went there on the 6th of August?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: I may have, but I can't remember. It was in my area of responsibility, but I don't remember specifically.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Did those houses that had "Croatian house" on it, were they, in fact, burnt after that?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, did you look?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, you noted for us that you then went to Srb, and I continue on your statement. In your statement, going over on to the next page, on page 9, and you some dead individuals on the side of the road. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And some of those individuals had various forms of camouflage on, didn't they?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So you don't know whether or not those people were civilians or soldiers, do you?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I do not know, but I do know that there was some women there that did not have any camouflage on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, you saw vehicles that had also been shot. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was small arms fire to the vehicles.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: In addition to ARSK vehicles, isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean, ARSK, as military vehicles?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember seeing military -- I can remember sing the ambiguous Yugo there; you know, the one that looks like Volkswagen Rabbit.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: You note in your statement that you saw abandoned ARSK military equipment?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that was -- I believe I am referring to a tank.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Okay. Pardon me. That's a vehicle, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: I guess I was thinking more of a passenger vehicle.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: At this location -- do you know what a fighting withdrawal is?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm familiar with the term.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Do you have any idea whether or not as the Serb population was withdrawing with the ARSK if they were fighting as they were withdrawing?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wasn't there. I wouldn't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So to round this out, Mr. Dawes, you have no -- again you have no information as to how these individuals were killed?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: None.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, you told us that you went out with Andries Dreyer on the 6th, and what you have told us this Trial Chamber, and is in your reports, you believe are significant events that you believe needed to be told to the Office of the Prosecutor and the Chamber. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: About that trip?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let me put to you P72, page 6, paragraph 20. Mr. Dawes, this is the statement given to the Office of the Prosecutor by Andries Dreyer recounting what took place on the 6th. And without reading it aloud, you can note that Mr. Dreyer says nothing about any trip to Vrbnik, Kistanje, or Srb on the 6th.

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can read that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And I put to you, sir, how it is that an event of such significance in your mind could have bypassed, or possibly bypassed, Mr. Dreyer in a time when there was such a restriction of movement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Russo.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Your Honour, I will object. That calls for pure speculation as to the workings of Mr. Dreyer's mind.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I take it that -- this is an item that the Prosecution has put into evidence --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's see --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: -- and I offered him an opportunity to explain.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Dawes, would there be anything, to your knowledge, which would explain why Mr. Dreyer has not mentioned this trip; whereas, you gave extensive evidence on it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I could speculate, Your Honour, but it would be speculation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, we're not seeking speculation, but usually based on something. Is there anything in your knowledge which would the basis of what you want to present as your speculation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I believe Mr. Dreyer is still currently an UN worker. On August the 6th, we were allowed to enter into the town of Knin, but we were not allowed to go on a sightseeing trip.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. What you say is that the fact that you are not allowed to make this trip may have been at the basis of not referring to it in the report. Is that it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You relate this to the fact that you did something you were not allowed to do.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed, Mr. Kehoe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So, just taking that answer, that based on the fact that he was not allowed, that that was the reason why he didn't describe this trip to Kistanje. Is that your statement?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know if that could be my statement, but that is what I'm speculating.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, they weren't supposed to go into Knin either, were they -- were you?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I believe we were allowed to go into Knin on the 6th.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: There was restriction of movements to go in Knin.

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is different levels of restriction of movement specifically with an UN security officer.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Turn to page 6 - page 8, last paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very last paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Third-to last paragraph: "Andries succeeded in getting through the main gate by telling the Jordanian camp guard about his security business?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. So if Andries was conducting security business in Knin, I believe he would have been allowed to be in Knin. He was a security guy, after all. Again, I am speculating.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: But, in fact, he was going Knin to check on his personal item, right?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: We did that on the roundabout part of the trip.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Isn't it a fact, Mr. Dawes, that the only place that you went on the 6th was to Knin with Mr. Dreyer? Isn't that a fact?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not a fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, let us turn, sir, if we can, to the situation report for UN Sector South. This is just one of many, and this is of the 6th.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: This is P351, to show the first page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, and let us turn to the fourth page in. You do note that Captain Hill was permitted to go to Knin, don't you?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't -- yes. It would stand to reason that he would be allowed to go to Knin, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And in the centre of that page is discussing Captain Hill, and I'm talking about point B under HQ Sector South, where it talks about Mr. Hill going into Knin, and midway through, says that: "OC MP PL entered buildings looking for evidence of looting and destruction ..."

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Officer in charge is military police platoon."

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Just reading it literally: "... and found little evidence of ransacking or wanton destruction. What looting there is seems limited to beer and portable radios," and it goes on to discuss the situation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. It reads also "et cetera," after the --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I put to you, sir, there is nothing in this report about your trip to Kistanje or Srb or Vrbnik. Who did you report this to?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: The Chamber, on this score, on the 6th --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And I don't want to mislead the Court that this is the only report of the 6th. In the 6th, there is P348, 349, 350, 351, 352. On the 7th, there is sitreps, 353, 354, 355.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: In all of these sitreps, over the course of two days, Mr. Dawes, there is no reflection whatsoever of your trip to Kistanje, Srb, and Vrbnik and what you observed, and I want to explain to this Chamber why.

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot tell you why.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If I might have one moment, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Your Honour, I trust I'm within my time-frame, and I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Kehoe. I'm looking at the other Defence counsel to see if the situation is still the same. Mr. Kay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I have no questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Same, Your Honour, no questions. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Russo, is there any need for further re-examination of the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Mr. Dawes, let me go, first, to the last question you were just asked. You have already indicated to the Court that you were not permitted to take the trip you took on the 6th of August outside of Knin. Can you tell the Court whether, given the fact that you were not allowed to do that, you would have submitted an official report indicating that you had?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I would not have submitted a official report.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I object. I object. That is counter to what he just said. He said he told people in the headquarters. That's what he said in cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Your Honour, he may have told people who were in headquarters; that doesn't mean he filed an official report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is that what he said, that he told, or that he assumed that? Let me just see. Could you give me the page and line reference, Mr. Kehoe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... Mr. Misetic is pulling it up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. It's my recollection that he said something of the kind: It would be logical to assume.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That, of course, is not the same as what you now say. "He told" is not the same as "I assume" or "it would be logical," which means a reconstruction rather than actual knowledge; and reporting and telling, of course, is not exactly the same. Mr. Russo.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Mr. Dawes, you were asked yesterday regarding one of your neighbours who had an anti-aircraft weapon in his backyard, and I believe you indicated that that was at one of your earlier accommodations in Knin. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: That would have been the first two months of living in Knin.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: What time-frame would that have been?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would have to check back through the records to find out when I first arrived Knin, but it would have been in the first two months of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: You can check the first page of your first statement. I believe it indicates your tour of duty?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: From May, so it was my first residence, soit would have been May, May/June, potentially part of July, of 1994.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And can you tell the Court when the last time you saw this anti-aircraft weapon was?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: It would have been while I was living there.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: I believe you also indicated that he had used this anti-aircraft weapon to fire at drones. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe I said that would be possible that he would have fired on drones. I remember him firing it off just at the end of football games and basketball games myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Can you tell the Court whether you ever saw him of firing at any kind of aircraft?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you. You were also asked, Mr. Dawes, about the dead civilians that you saw, or what you said were dead civilians, on the streets and sidewalks of downtown Knin on your first trip on 4 August. I believe Mr. Kehoe was asking whether or not you knew if any of those males were part of the RSK or not. I'd like to you tell the Court whether you saw any dead females on the streets of Knin?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And with respect to the dead males that you saw, can you tell the Court whether all of them, some of them, or none of them had on a full military uniform?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: None of them had a full military uniform, but some of them had partially military uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Are you able to tell the Court whether any of the dead people you saw had any weaponry in or around their person?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not recall seeing any weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: You were also asked, Mr. Dawes, about the 12 to 15 ARSK soldiers that you saw in Potkonje during one of your trips on the 4th of August, and I'd like you to tell the Court whether or not there was any shelling of Potkonje while you were there.

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was no direct shelling of Potkonje. The shelling was in the general area of that area, but not on the village itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And are you able to tell the Court whether these 12 or 15 ARSK soldiers appeared to you to be operating as a unit or otherwise?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were in complete panic as to what to do with themselves, and their first -- I believe their first order of business -- well, their first logical thought, I guess, was to kidnap a bunch of unarmed UN observers, to take them hostage. So I would -- I would say to you that they were acting in an unmilitary-like manner.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you. You were also asked about the four ARSK trucks you had seen on the 4th of August, carrying lightly wounded soldiers; and you marked for the Defence, on an aerial photograph of Knin, the direction in which they were going. I'd like to take you to there. It's page 6 of your first statement, and I don't know --

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: I'm not sure, Your Honour, but if we call up that exhibit that he marked and then put additional markings on it, if that can be submitted as a subsequent exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That can be admitted as a subsequent exhibit, Madam Registrar, if I'm not mistaken. So we call it up and then it will be stored again with additional markings. That's what you suggest.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Thank you. In that event, I would ask for Madam Registrar to call up D864.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. It's similar to P62, which is, of course, a basic document to which markings were added.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Mr. Dawes, looking at page 6 of your statement, and it's at the bottom of that first full paragraph, where you indicate that: "Just before we left the area, we saw four ARSK truck with lightly wounded personnel coming from the direction of the Strmica road." It says, "the ... passed us just outside of the POL station, and we had to pull over the APC to let them pass. They went in the direction north-west. At the junction just before the main road, I met a few ARSK soldiers from the so-called ear-ring brigade." If you could indicate on the map which is now on your screen, I would ask for the court usher's assistance to mark in red, the portion where you say that they passed you just outside the POL station; and when you say they went in the direction north-west, if you could indicated on this map where you meant they were going north-west.

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certainly. I'll mark first the POL station, and then your second question was the general direction they were travelling up to, Mr. Russo?

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: If I could have this image admitted, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No objection, I take it. Madam Registrar, the already marked document with additional markings that would be ...

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That would be Exhibit P984, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P984 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Mr. Dawes, you were shown a number of reports --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Excuse me, excuse me. Just clarification, Judge, I think that came as 984, but I take it - correct me if I'm wrong, Mr. Russo - I think that one of your aerials with the witness's markings was 984.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's not entirely clear to me. I think P62 was marked in relation to what the witness observed, I think, people arriving from the Strmica area, if I'm not mistaken. The witness explain what we could not see on this map was the cross-roads just east of that, and he indicated the direction.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Maybe I'm not the clear, Judge. I think that 984 has already been received in evidence, and I think we just received this over no objection as P984.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but there are additional markings on it, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think Mr. Kehoe is attempting to say that the number should be P985.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P985, if that is the case, then I have no ...

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe is correct, Your Honours. Registry stands corrected.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I am honoured.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then it's P985. But it's the picture you want to have on the screen, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: That's correct, Judge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You asked for P984, and Madam Registrar knew what the needs were, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Actually, that is not correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Oh, perhaps I'm lost. If the parties have no problems at this moment anymore, then I'll --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: That's good, Judge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- I'll just render. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Mr. Dawes, you were shown a number of documents with respect to the collection and inventory of what has been called war booty, including televisions, apparently DVD players.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And just for the Court's benefit, I believe at that time laser disc players were in existence, simply very large looking CDs.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I'm not taking that crap. That is Mr. Misetic's deal.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And what I'd like to ask you with respect to the items that you were referred to in those documents as having been seized by the military police. What I'd like to ask you is: At any check-points, did you ever see anyone, either civilian or military, being arrested for carrying looted items?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And somewhere in there, you also indicated that you saw HV soldiers confiscating items, and I wasn't clear about what you meant by that. Were these soldiers confiscating items from certain people, or did you mean that term to include something else?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe Mr. Kehoe used that word "confiscating," and I sort of followed on with it. What I meant was that the Croatian soldiers were taking items from houses.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I seek further clarification in that respect. I think you were talking about apartment buildings where they were piled in front of those buildings, is that right; or did you also see piles of goods before, for example, barracks or government buildings or police stations?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sir, I saw items being taken out of different military installations, yes; but specific to what I think Mr. Russo is talking about was civilian apartment buildings where Croatian soldiers were seen removing items. Is that clear?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So you saw that -- well, let me just have a look. Yes. When you say Croatian soldiers were taking items from houses, that's where you referred to apartment buildings, civilian premises.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But you also saw, as you told us, goods being taken from, let's say, official buildings.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And just to further clarify on that issue, can you say - if you can recall - whether or not you saw televisions, DVD players, all of those things, being taken out of official installations?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: For the record, I never saw a DVD player in the RSK. What was your question again? I'm fixated on the DVD player.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: As are apparently the rest of the people in the courtroom. Let's just stick to televisions for now. Can you tell the Court whether or not you saw televisions, or let's include also stereos, being removed from official installations?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, you were also were questioned with respect to your observations in Vrbnik on the 6th of August, where you indicated that you saw a few HV soldiers carrying TV sets and such other items; and you were asked whether or not you had any idea if they were cataloguing or selecting war booty. You did mention - and this appears at transcript page 10.405, from lines 21 to 24 - you made a distinction between what you had observed in Vrbnik and Kistanje versus what you had observed in Knin, calling what you observed in Vrbnik and Kistanje "disorganised" versus what you saw in Knin as "organised." I would like to you please explain why you made a distinction between what you saw in Vrbnik and what you saw in Knin.

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Vrbnik -- and I apologise for my lack of better words that I could be using from the military perspective. Vrbnik was very unorganized. It was happenstance. People were -- soldiers were walking in and out of buildings taking items, not putting them in different piles, so a pile of TVs, a pile of stereos, a pile of personal belongings. It was chaotic. It wasn't as organised as it was in Knin where there was definitely a -- law and order was prevailing. There was command and control of the situation where items were being placed into different piles, so furniture, TVs, stereos, and appliances. Then items of what I call no value, clothing, were dumped into huge piles at the front of the streets for removal.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you. The last issue I'd like to address is what you observed at the intersection for Srb on the return trip to Knin on the 6th of August. You were asked some questions about that by Mr. Kehoe as to whether or not you saw any ARSK military vehicles. I'd like to refer to you page 9 of your first statement, and you can look to the middle of the page where you're discussing what you see in Kistanje. You indicate you were only there for 15 minutes, and then you say: "I didn't see one civilian in Kistanje that day, neither saw I any civilian Croatian car. All cars were either abandoned Serb cars or HV army vehicles." Then you indicate that you drove the main road back to Knin, and you say: "At the intersection to Srb, we noticed lots of splay damages on the road and lots of abandoned civilian Serb cars with damages after, not shelling but small arms fire." During Mr. Kehoe's question, you did mention that you had seen an ARSK tank somewhere. I would like you to clarify for the Court whether at that particular intersection, where you saw these dead civilians, did you see any military vehicles at that particular intersection?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not at that particular intersection.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And are you able to tell the Court approximately how far from that intersection you saw the first ARSK military vehicle?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Accurately, no. I could not tell you the distance. It was not immediately close to the intersection, and it wasn't in the direction of Knin. It was on the direction towards Kistanje.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: I have no further questions, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Judge Gwaunza has one or more questions for you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GWAUNZA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Dawes. Can I take you back to your statement of 1996, page 11, the third paragraph. In the middle, it will says: "Every time a contract was closed and a facility handed over, the house, or whatever it was, was destroyed, either blown up or a tap broken so that water made the destruction." My question is: Would you know why these properties were destroyed and did you actually witness this happening?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: To answer your question, Your Honour, I did not see who did this destruction. This was mainly in the Canadian AOR. Was there any other question asked that I didn't answer?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GWAUNZA
utterances.text: Yes. I asked whether you knew why this was done, whether you actually witnessed it happening.

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't witness it happening, and I don't know why it was done.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GWAUNZA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Since I have no further questions for you, Mr. Dawes, any need for further questions by the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: On this situation with the anti-aircraft weapon, and returning to page 10.435, line 1, I asked you this question, and did you give this answer: "Now, Mr. Dawes, you mentioned that your neighbour fired it at football games. He also fired it at aircraft that was passing over head, didn't he? "A. It is an anti-aircraft weapon, so I would probably say yes. "Q. Well, did he not fire it at drones that were flying about the area? "A. That was standard protocol for the Serbs to fire at drones."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then I intervened.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... intervened. I think I said --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I asked you whether you heard or whether you saw such firing, apparently related to drones.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then you confirmed that you did, and that's a bit different from what you told us today.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sir, I cannot remember that specific anti-aircraft gun-firing at drones, but it was standard. I did see Serbs fire at drones at other locations, but not that specific anti-aircraft site.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: You noted for us that -- in response to questions by Mr. Russo, that you hadn't seen the weapons since you moved out of that area. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Did he get rid of it?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. Probably not, it was a pretty valuable piece of kit.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So that pretty valuable piece of kit, as far as you know, was there until Operation Storm. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: As far as you know.

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Now, let's go back to P985.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: This is the chart that you put in just now with Mr. Russo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, perhaps I could clarify. Earlier I said: "I render." I meant at that time: "I surrender." As a matter of fact, in my efforts to again demonstrate that the Registry is always right, I may have made a mistake, so I'm blaming myself, because finally I think I said that P984 was admitted into evidence, then we had a discussion about P985, and I did not declare that having been admitted into evidence, which I do now. So we're now at P985 which is in evidence. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Your Honour, we won't call it a mistake but an oversight. It's much gentler.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Taking a look at P985, this is the direction those four trucks were going in. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Were you aware or do you know whether or not these soldiers were moving towards the area of Bulina Strana to prepare for the defence of Knin?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know where that location is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, are you are -- you were aware of the munitions depot on the other side of the road that you weren't permitted to go into?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely. Is that what you're talking about?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: In that general area.

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is quite feasible that they could have turned down that road to go there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. Russo asked you questions about arrests for looting. As you sit here, sir, you have no knowledge about any arrests for looting or for seized items by the military police, do you?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I do not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, changing subjects to going through the houses that you noted HV soldiers were taking items out of houses. Now, were you aware that soldiers, ARSK soldiers, had been living in those houses?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Were you aware that during one of these searches of one of these houses -- apartment buildings, that the HV seized a Zolja rocket from an ARSK soldier in one of those houses -- one were those apartment buildings?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I was not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: You would expect the HV to take that item, wouldn't you?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So it would be accurate to say that when you saw HV soldiers going into individual apartments throughout Knin, you have no knowledge who was living in that apartment, specifically you have no knowledge if it was an ARSK soldier or not?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just the houses that UN civilians were living in, I just have knowledge of those houses.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So the answer is with regard to for instance any type of high-rise, you have no knowledge of who was living in those individual places?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, on the situation with Vrbnik, the items that you saw seized, I mean you have no knowledge whether or not those were, in fact, seized by the military police or were registered in a similar manner as we've seen from these document, do you?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I do not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Kehoe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour. Just one follow-up question, if I may, relating to questions that were just asked.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You didn't use your right to cross-examine the witness, but let not be over-formalistic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I appreciate that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Dawes, you talked about check-points. You left Sector South on August 10th for two weeks; correct?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct, in and around that date.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: At least it's referenced in your first statement, P80 [sic], on page 11, that: "On the 10th of August, I left Sector South for Canada for two weeks because of medical reasons." Correct?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: In that time-frame, how many days -- I think you said you were out of the UN Sector South camp twice, between the time of Operation Storm until the time you left on August 10th, am I correct or was it more than that?

utterances.speaker: MURRAY DOUGLAS DAWES [Resumed]
